text:
Alex: RFC: proposing SLO-driven routing + circuit-breaker thresholds per customer tier. Need quick sync on policy shape & console UX before next sprint.
Maria: +1. Can you sketch the high-level mapping you have in mind?
Alex: Thinking Tier -> {p95_latency_ms, availability_pct} + CB rules that trigger fallbacks. Example: Gold p95=100ms, 99.9% availability; Silver p95=250ms, 99.5%; Bronze p95=600ms, 99.0%.
Jon: Those numbers look reasonable as defaults. We should also consider sustained vs spike behavior: CB should look at a rolling 1m and 5m window.
Sam: Important: fallback ordering. Should we try (1) same model lower-precision variant, (2) smaller model family, (3) region fallback, (4) queue/degrade? Need deterministic policy.
Lina: From UX: console should surface the active policy and show predicted cost/latency impact of each fallback step. Users freak out if we silently switch models.
Maria: Agree. Also need telemetry: per-route p50/p95/p99, error-rate, fallback-counts, CB-open-duration. UI graph + annotations when a CB fired.
Jon: Proposal for CB triggers: open when (error_rate >= 5% for >= 60s) OR (p95 >= 2x target for 120s). Close when both error_rate < 2% and p95 <= 1.2x target for 5m. Thoughts?
Alex: I like explicit multipliers. Maybe make the multipliers configurable per tier (Gold more aggressive).
Sam: API shape debate: 2 options: (A) policy object attached to customer profile with tier defaults + per-route overrides, or (B) route-centric policy that references customer tier. Which is easier for rollouts?
Maria: For rollouts UX, route-centric is friendlier: teams can A/B per-route. But for enterprise customers with org-wide SLAs, customer-profile policies are needed. We should support both, with clear precedence.
Lina: UX note: show precedence in the console header. If a customer-level SLO overrides route-level, show a banner: "Customer SLO enforced" with link to edit.
Jon: Telemetry cost: storing per-request p95/p99 across every route at high res is heavy. We should aggregate to 10s/1m buckets and store fallback counters as separate metrics.
Alex: Good point. We'll expose high-res on-demand for a short retention window and aggregated longer-term.
Maria: Quotas interplay: if we fallback to smaller model, token cost changes. Rollout preview should estimate token-cost delta and billing impact.
Sam: Also need to decide whether CB triggers count requests that were already routed to a fallback model. If fallback fails too, we could get a loop. Add a guard to not re-trigger fallback to the same variant.
Jon: Implementation detail: we should tag requests with routing_decision metadata: tier, policy_id, fallback_step to make telemetry downstream easier.
Alex: Example policy JSON I'd propose we put in the repo:
```json
{
  "policy_id": "tiered-slo-v1",
  "defaults": {
    "Gold": {"p95_ms": 100, "availability_pct": 99.9},
    "Silver": {"p95_ms": 250, "availability_pct": 99.5},
    "Bronze": {"p95_ms": 600, "availability_pct": 99.0}
  },
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "open_conditions": [
      {"metric":"error_rate","threshold_pct":5,"window_s":60},
      {"metric":"p95_ms","multiplier":2,"window_s":120}
    ],
    "close_conditions": {"error_rate_pct":2,"p95_multiplier":1.2,"hold_s":300}
  },
  "fallback_order": ["quantized_variant","small_model","region_fallback","degrade_fastpath"],
  "max_fallback_per_min": 5
}
```
Maria: +1. We should add a recommended presets section in the UI: "production-recommended", "cost-optimized", "latency-optimized". Lina can design.
Lina: I'll mock presets. Quick Q: should presets be editable copies or live links to presets? I vote editable copies to avoid surprising changes.
Sam: For API, suggest endpoints: POST /policies (create), GET /policies/{id}, PATCH /policies/{id}, and POST /policies/{id}/preview with sample workload to return predicted impacts.
Jon: On the runtime: add an internal circuit-breaker telemetry event that emits when CB enters OPEN/CLOSED/HALF_OPEN with reason & snapshot metrics. That will make incident triage much easier.
Alex: Ops question: how do we test this in staging without impacting prod? Feature flag the routing policy evaluation and run in shadow mode for 48h, then small canary.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-policy-feature-flag -> staging at 2026-03-19T03:00Z (sha: a1b2c3).
Maria: Next steps: (1) Sam + Jon implement runtime & telemetry hooks (2) Lina builds mockups + presets (3) Alex + I will draft console copy and rollout wizard flow (4) schedule shadow run for 48h.
Jon: I'll add the CB open/close events to our tracing schema and create a dashboard template (p95, error_rate, fallback_count, cb_state timeline).
Sam: I'll start an RFC PR with the policy schema and a small emulator to simulate load + trigger CB logic.
Alex: Great. If nobody objects, we'll lock defaults and put tasks into the sprint planning board. Objections within 24h?
Maria: No objections from me.
Lina: No objections. I'll start design.
Jon: Looks good.
Sam: Fine by me.
Alex: Cool — thanks everyone.
